## What clicked

**Fat isn't hydrophobic — water is fat-phobic.** Water molecules can't form hydrogen bonds with nonpolar tails, so around each tail they have to arrange themselves into an ordered "cage" and lose their freedom of movement (entropy). It's more favorable for water to push all the nonpolar molecules into one cluster, which shrinks the surface it has to organize around. The oil doesn't avoid water; water squeezes the oil out. Fat-shaming at the molecular level.

## Where I got stuck

**Stat 110, Strategic Practice 1 — pretty much everywhere.** Dice, palindromes, poker hands, lattice paths, words without repeated letters, story proofs: I got stuck at almost every step of every problem and couldn't have solved any of them without hints. Counting turned out to be a completely different way of thinking from anything I'd done before. Each problem needs its own way of looking at it, and I don't have a toolbox for that yet.

What worked was taking one hint at a time and then trying the next step myself. It was slow, but by the end, I could at least see which questions to ask: does order matter, am I counting something twice, can I count the complement instead?

## What I'm changing

- **Stat 110 problems in shorter, more frequent sessions.** Long sessions on counting problems left me stuck and frustrated. Starting next week, I'm switching from three 40-minute sessions to six 20-minute ones: less time to spiral on a single step, more chances to come back with fresh eyes.
- **Back to basic chemistry.** Biochemistry kept assuming things I didn't remember from school: electronegativity, ionic and covalent bonds, polarity, hydrogen bonds. Alongside the main courses, I'm spending time on the basics with Crash Course Chemistry and Khan Academy.
- **Calculus starts.** The next course on my route is Differential and Integral Calculus, so derivatives and integrals join the weekly plan.
